pois.name: Ueno Park
pois.description: Tokyo's most celebrated public park — 53 hectares housing the national museum, zoo, 5 art museums, and the most famous hanami (cherry blossom) avenue in Japan. 1,200 somei-yoshino trees bloom late March, drawing 2 million visitors in two weeks.

pois.name: Tokyo National Museum
pois.description: Japan's oldest and largest museum (founded 1872), housing 110,000 artefacts — samurai armour, ukiyo-e prints, Buddhist sculpture, and the world's largest collection of Japanese art. The Honkan main building (1938) is a masterpiece of Imperial Crown architectural style.

pois.name: Ueno Zoological Gardens
pois.description: Japan's oldest zoo (1882), home to two giant pandas (Lili and Xiaoxiao, born 2021) — the most-visited animals in the country. Split across two sections connected by a monorail, with 3.5 million annual visitors.
pois.name: Tokyo National Museum
pois.description: Japan's oldest and largest museum (1872). Houses 110,000+ artifacts including samurai swords, ukiyo-e prints, and the famous Great Buddha statue. The Honkan (Japanese Gallery) is a designated Important Cultural Property.

pois.name: Ueno Station
pois.description: Major JR terminal (1883) serving the Tohoku Shinkansen, Joban Line, and Yamanote loop. Historically the 'gateway to the north' — generations of migrants from Tohoku and Hokkaido arrived here. The park-side exit opens directly onto the cherry-blossom avenue.

pois.name: Ameya-Yokocho (Ameyoko)
pois.description: Post-war black-market alley (ameya = candy seller) that became a 500-stall open-air market beneath the JR Yamanote tracks. Fresh seafood, dried goods, cosmetics and sneakers — Tokyo's loudest and most chaotic market. Unmissable during New Year's Eve shopping.

description: Historic station opened in 1883. Major hub for JR Yamanote, Keihin-Tohoku, and Shinkansen lines. The iconic red-brick facade (designed by Kingo Tatsuno) was restored in 2012.

partnerURL.name: Ueno Park
partnerURL.description: Japan's first public park (1873). 500+ cherry trees bloom in late March–early April. Home to 8 museums, Ueno Zoo (Japan's oldest, 1882), and Shinobazu Pond with its Bentendo Temple.

partnerURL.name: Shinobazu Pond
partnerURL.description: Large freshwater pond in Ueno Park. Rent rowboats in summer, see lotus flowers in July–August. The Bentendo Temple on an island is dedicated to Benzaiten, goddess of water and music.

partnerURL.name: Ameya Yokocho
partnerURL.description: Vibrant market street stretching from Ueno Station to Okachimachi. 400+ shops selling fresh seafood, spices, cosmetics, and street food. The atmosphere is chaotic, colorful, and authentically Tokyo.

partnerURL.name: Ueno Zoo
partnerURL.description: Japan's oldest zoo (1882). Famous for its giant pandas (gift from China in 1972), Sumatran tigers, and the historic 'Garden of Flowers and Birds' monorail (Japan's first, 1952).
